text.p: Barrick Gold Corp said on Monday that its cash flow, earnings and dividends were protected by a large hedge position and low-cost earnings.

"Barrick is fully protected with the largest hedge position and the lowest operating costs in the industry," Chief Executive Peter Munk said in a statement. "Our cash flow, earnings and dividends are unaffected through the year 2000 despite the present turmoil."
Barrick said its hedge position ensured a minimum average price of US$420 an ounce for its production, with cash operating costs of under US$200 an ounce.
Barrick said it was concerned about the impact of the decline in gold prices on the industry, but believed the price fall did not reflect long-term fundamental supply and demand factors.

The gold price fell sharply after news last week that the Reserve Bank of Australia (Australia's central bank) sold 167 tonnes of gold reserves over the past six months. Gold fixed in London at US$318.75 an ounce today, near 12-year lows.
Gold has lost more than 13 percent of its value this year as central banks review the worth of holding reserves.
Barrick was down C$0.60 to C$27.60 in third most active trading today on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
